newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA OVERCOME MEXICO IN TUMULTUOUS SEMI-FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA OVERCOME MEXICO IN TUMULTUOUS SEMI-FINAL.

text.p: Bolivia beat Mexico 3-1 Wednesday in a Copa America semi-final littered with hugely controversial refereeing decisions, one of which led to Mexican protests that held up the game for ten minutes.

Mexico, who finished a tumultuous match with nine players after having two sent off, were livid at Bolivia's first goal, which wiped out an early Mexican lead. The Mexicans claimed that the ball had not crossed the line.

The Mexicans also had a penalty claim turned down when they were leading 1-0 and the free kick from which Bolivia scored their crucial second goal appeared to be wrongly awarded by Paraguayan referee Epifanio Gonzalez.
After the Bolivian equaliser, Mexico's players surrounded the referee while team officials, including coach Bora Milutinovic, ran onto the field to protest and were surrounded by riot police.
Play was delayed until the protests subsided, which only happened after ten minutes of wrangling between officials, the referee, the police and the Mexicans.
Mexico had been given little chance of winning because of the little time they had to adapt to the altitude of La Paz, 3,600 metres above sea level.
But they stunned a 39,000 home crowd when Nicolas Ramirez scored in the fifth minute from a free kick which was deflected into the goal by the Bolivian wall.

The Mexicans were aggrieved from the 25th minute when striker Luis Hernandez, the competition's top scorer with five goals, was tripped in the penalty area by Juan Manuel Pena only for the referee to wave play on.

One minute later, Erwin Sanchez equalised with a dipping, swerving free kick from 35 metres which bounced off the underside of the crossbar and then out of the goal. Despite the protests which followed, television replays later showed that referee Gonzalez was right to give the goal, as the ball crossed the line before bouncing back into play.

Bolivia went ahead in the 44th minute -- effectively the 34th minute after the interruption -- when Ramiro Castillo scored following a free kick, awarded for an alleged foul by the Mexican defence on the same player.
Replays showed, however, that Castillo had not been touched when he went tumbling on the edge of the area in the incident that led to the free kick.
Mexico were angry again shortly afterwards when defender Claudio Suarez, who had earlier been booked, was sent off for a foul, even though he appeared to play the ball.

Bolivia, outplayed for much of the game, rode their luck throughout and could have been 3-0 behind before their equaliser as the dangerous Mexicans created several early chances. The best effort was Pavel Pardo's rasping shot which hit the crossbar.
Castillo's goal was hugely fortuituous as he was looking the other way when Marco Etcheverry's free kick, which had been going side, struck him and flew into the net.

Mexico kept pressing in the second half but Jaime Moreno settled the game in the 75th minute when he broke clear of the Mexican defence and chipped the ball over Adolfo Rios. Joel Sanchez, who had earlier been booked, was sent off for sliding into Moreno as he scored.
Moreno was taken off injured and replaced by Mauro Blanco.
Bolivia, who have won the Copa America only once before, will face Brazil or Peru, who meet in the other semi-final Thursday in Santa Cruz, in Sunday's final.
Mexico had played their quarter-final against Ecuador on Sunday and arrived in La Paz just hours before the game in an attempt to reduce the affects of the high altitude.
